Analog-Finder

Where on Earth looks most like a landing site on the Moon or Mars? The map compares 101,580 land cells (20 arcminutes each, about 37 km) with the fingerprint of the target site across ten dimensions.

    Method and limits

    For each dimension, 100 points means identical to the target site and 0 points means as unlike it as the least similar land on Earth (2nd to 98th percentile). The total score is the weighted mean. Where the target value lies outside what Earth offers, no cell reaches 100 points. That is intended: for temperature and air pressure the number shows how far the analogy holds.

    Data

    • Earth, terrain: ETOPO1 (NOAA), 10 arcminutes. Slope over an 18.5 km baseline, relief as the spread of elevation over about 90 km.
    • Mars, terrain: MOLA spherical harmonic model MarsTopo719, limited to the same wavelength as the Earth data, flattening removed.
    • Moon, terrain: LOLA topography, 10 arcminutes, band-limited in the same way.
    • Earth, climate: WorldClim 2.1, mean annual temperature and annual precipitation (1970 to 2000).
    • Earth, vegetation: NASA MODIS/Terra MOD13C2 (version 061), annual mean NDVI from all twelve months of 2023. Missing values on land count as bare.
    • Earth, albedo: NASA MODIS MCD43C3 (version 061), shortwave, the 15th of each month in 2023. Snow-covered months are left out where snow-free months exist.
    • Earth, apparent thermal inertia: (1 − albedo) divided by the day-night swing of surface temperature from NASA MODIS/Aqua MYD11C3 (version 061, all twelve months of 2023, overpasses at about 13:30 and 01:30 local time). Low values mean loose, dry, dusty ground that heats and cools fast.
    • The target values for albedo and thermal inertia on the Moon and Mars are still rough estimates. They will be replaced by TES and Diviner measurements.
    • Air pressure from elevation (standard atmosphere), sun elevation from latitude and axial tilt, ground ice as a permafrost estimate from mean annual temperature.
    • Earth, land cover filter: NASA MODIS MCD12C1 (version 061, 2023). Cells that are more than half water, forest, cropland or urban are removed, which drops 31% of the ice-free land cells.
    • Glaciers, ice shelves, region and country names: Natural Earth.

    What this prototype cannot do

    • The 18.5 km baseline describes landscape types, not landing sites. Rover-scale slopes need elevation models at metre resolution.
    • Mineralogy (EMIT, ASTER), dust (MERRA-2) and the subsurface, such as lava tubes, are missing. These are the next dimensions.
    • Ground ice is estimated from temperature and is therefore coupled to it. A real permafrost map would be better.
    • Gravity, vacuum, radiation and the thin CO₂ atmosphere cannot be reproduced anywhere on Earth.
